subject: arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_lpi2c.c: Cleanups and error fixes
label: missing
evidence: Besides cleanup, the listed hunk rewrites the error path of imx9_lpi2c_isr_process, which is what the commit message means by 'handle error cases properly': on any LPI2C_MSR_ERROR_MASK bit the new code clears the TX and RX FIFOs (LPI2C_MCR_RTF | LPI2C_MCR_RRF), clears all error flags, sets msgc and dcnt to 0 and then sends STOP or ends the transfer, whereas the old code only recorded the status, sent STOP when I2C_M_NOSTOP was clear and cleared NDF/ALF/FEF/EPF. imxrt_lpi2c_isr_process is the old imx9 handler line for line (a whitespace-insensitive diff of the two functions differs only in the DMA channel names, and imxrt_lpi2c_sem_waitdone likewise matches the old imx9 version): its error branch (lines 1582-1603) leaves dcnt, msgc, the FIFOs and the TDIE/RDIE enables untouched, so later TDF/RDF interrupts go back through the normal branch, which keeps writing bytes while dcnt > 0 and starts the next message at line 1512, and the waiting thread is woken only when EPF and SDF are seen together (line 1616). Nothing else in the imxrt driver ends a failed transfer early: imxrt_lpi2c_transfer only checks priv->status after the wait, and this interrupt path is the default because IMXRT_LPI2C_DMA defaults to n. Every bit the 08949dec version uses (LPI2C_MCR_RTF/RRF, LPI2C_MSR_ERROR_MASK, EPF/SDF, the MIER bits, LPI2C_MTDR_CMD_STOP) is defined for imxrt, and the current imx9 handler still flushes the FIFOs and zeroes the counts on error; only a later imx9 refinement (3afa58cdd) switched to LPI2C_MCFG0_ABORT, which imxrt does not define. Confidence is medium because the commit message names no concrete failure, the bus-level effect depends on controller behaviour the repository does not document, and parts of the rewrite (message chaining, ignoring NACK on the last RX byte) are design changes rather than this fix.

title: The imxrt LPI2C interrupt handler does not end a transfer on a NACK or lost arbitration, so later interrupts can keep sending the remaining bytes and messages.
summary: In September 2024 the imx9 LPI2C driver (commit 08949dec, 'Cleanups and error fixes') rewrote its interrupt handler so that on an error it flushes the TX/RX FIFOs, clears all error flags, zeroes the remaining message and byte counts and ends the transfer, sending STOP if none was seen. The imxrt LPI2C driver still has the old handler: on NACK or lost arbitration it records the status, queues STOP only if the message lacks I2C_M_NOSTOP and clears the flags, but leaves the counts, FIFOs and TX/RX interrupts as they are and wakes the caller only when end-of-packet and STOP are seen together. As a result, after an error later interrupts can keep queuing the remaining bytes and start the next messages on the bus, and with I2C_M_NOSTOP no STOP is sent, so the caller may only get a timeout instead of a quick error. The exact bus effect depends on controller behaviour the repository does not document, and the imx9 rewrite also changed how messages are chained and was refined by later commits (one uses an ABORT bit imxrt does not define), so only the error-path part should be carried over, with testing on hardware.

subject: arch/arm/src/stm32h5/stm32_usbdrdhost.c: Disable host channel when freed
label: not_applicable
evidence: The selected hunk only adds forward declarations of stm32_set_chep_rx_status and stm32_set_chep_tx_status, which the STM32H5 USB DRD host driver needs so that its stm32_chan_free can set the channel's CHEP RX/TX status to disabled before freeing it ('Disable host channel when freed', 'Fixed by cancelling any transfers on free'). Those helpers program the DRD channel/endpoint register through USB_CHEP_* macros that are defined only in arch/arm/src/stm32h5/hardware/stm32_usbfs.h and used only by stm32_usbdrdhost.c; arch/arm/src/at32/at32_otgfshost.c is an OTG host driver that controls each channel through HCCHAR and has no CHEP register. subject: arch/arm/src/common/stm32: fix WWDG time left in WDIOC_GETSTATUS
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunk is the declaration half of the stm32_getstatus fix (elapsed/reload become remaining/counter for the new computation in the same function); the commit message says 'stm32_getstatus() returned the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft' and that 'the time left is the ticks above T_MAX scaled by the timeout'. gd32w51x_wwdgt.c uses the same window-watchdog scheme: gd32_start and gd32_keepalive load WWDGT_CTL_CNT_RESET | priv->reload, settimeout caps reload at WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX and sets timeout = 1000 * (reload + 1) / fwwdgt, and hardware/gd32w51x_wwdgt.h defines CNT_MASK 0x7f, CNT_MAX 0x3f and CNT_RESET 0x40, so the reset comes reload + 1 ticks after a reload, when the counter falls to CNT_MAX. Its gd32_getstatus, under the comment 'Get the time remaining', computes 'elapsed = priv->reload - (counter & WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX)', which for a counter between 0x40 and 0x40 | reload is the same value as the STM32 pre-fix '(WWDG_CR_T_RESET | priv->reload) - reload', and returns timeout * elapsed / (reload + 1) as timeleft, so it reports about 0 right after a keepalive and nearly the full timeout just before the reset. The macros the fix needs (WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MASK, WWDGT_CTL_CNT_SHIFT, WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX) all exist in the GD32W51x header, so nothing makes the fix inapplicable.

title: The GD32W51x window watchdog reports the elapsed time instead of the time left in WDIOC_GETSTATUS.
summary: On 2026-10-20 commit 14f2daaa2 fixed stm32_getstatus() in the STM32 WWDG driver, which returned the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft, by taking the counter value above WWDG_CR_T_MAX instead. The GD32W51x WWDGT driver, added on 2026-10-23 with the same counter scheme (loaded with CNT_RESET | reload, timeout of reload + 1 ticks), still computes 'elapsed = priv->reload - (counter & WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX)' and returns timeout * elapsed / (reload + 1) as timeleft. subject: arch/arm/stm32: Fix RNG read hang on seed or clock error.
label: fixed_differently
evidence: The commit fixes a read hang that happened because on SEIS or CEIS 'the interrupt handler returned without clearing the flag, so the interrupt fired forever and read() never returned'; the picked hunk (g_rngdev.rd_error = 0 in the read function) only resets the new error code that lets read() fail with -EIO after a clock error. subject: arch/arm/nrf52: fix the TX state handling
label: fixed_differently
evidence: The picked hunk changed nrf52_radioi8_txdelayed() so that a delayed (no-CSMA) frame arriving while a CSMA transaction is busy is kept pending and started later, instead of setting txdelayed_busy and returning -EBUSY, which the MAC ignores, so the frame 'was neither sent nor confirmed'. title: The ESP32-C2 Wi-Fi adapter allocates a new interrupt handle on every Wi-Fi start and leaks it because the IRQ already has one registered.
summary: On 2026-09-30 commit 1c6ed642b changed set_intr_wrapper in the esp32, esp32s2, esp32s3, esp32c3 and esp32c6 Wi-Fi adapters to reuse the interrupt handle already registered for the IRQ instead of allocating a new one each time. The ESP32-C2 adapter, added two weeks later, still has the old code: each call allocates a new handle from the kernel heap and passes it to esp_set_handle, which refuses it with -EINVAL because the handle from the first start is still registered, and the new block is never freed. An application that stops and restarts Wi-Fi on ESP32-C2 (for example to save power) therefore loses a few bytes of kernel heap per cycle without bound. The same patch applies with no changes; the only part not visible in the repository is the closed Wi-Fi library itself, whose repeated calls on every start are stated by the fix commit message.

subject: arch/xtensa/esp32s3: Don't overrun buffers in SPI poll exchange.
label: missing
evidence: The fix commit says esp32s3_spi_poll_exchange() always copies a full 32-bit word, so 'When the transfer length is not a multiple of 4, the last copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of txbuffer and writes up to 3 bytes past the end of rxbuffer, silently corrupting whatever follows the receive buffer in memory'; the picked hunk limits the final receive copy to chunk = MIN(sizeof(uint32_t), transfer_size - i). The esp32s2 esp32s2_spi_poll_exchange has the same structure: it computes total_bytes = nwords * (priv->nbits / 8), splits it into chunks of transfer_size = MIN(SPI_MAX_BUF_SIZE, bytes_remaining) with SPI_MAX_BUF_SIZE 64 (16 registers W0-W15), and its receive loop runs i in steps of sizeof(uintptr_t) up to transfer_size and does memcpy(rp, &r_wd, sizeof(uintptr_t)) for every step, so a final chunk whose length is not a multiple of 4 writes up to 3 bytes past the end of rxbuffer. Its transmit loop has the matching over-read (memcpy(&w_wd, tp, sizeof(uint32_t)) for every step), which the esp32s3 commit fixed in its other hunk. The function is reached from esp32s2_spi_exchange whenever SPI DMA is off, and with DMA on for every transfer at or below CONFIG_ESP32S2_SPI_DMATHRESHOLD (default 64), and nothing on the esp32s2 side pads or rounds the caller's buffers. The fix needs only MIN and the existing loop variables, both already used in this function, and esp32s2_spi.c has not been touched since the 2026-10-23 esp32s3 fix except for the exchange return type change.
title: The ESP32-S2 SPI polling exchange writes up to 3 bytes past the end of the receive buffer when the transfer length is not a multiple of 4.
summary: On 2026-10-23 commit 236b47dd0 changed the ESP32-S3 SPI polling exchange to copy only the bytes left in the last partial 32-bit word, after it was found corrupting the field after the receive buffer on a real board. The ESP32-S2 polling exchange is the same code: its receive loop still copies a full 4-byte word on every step, and its transmit loop still reads a full word from the transmit buffer. Any polled SPI transfer whose byte count is not a multiple of 4 (for example a 61-byte or 3-byte read, which goes through this path when DMA is off or the transfer is under the DMA threshold) therefore writes up to 3 bytes past the caller's receive buffer and reads up to 3 bytes past its transmit buffer, silently corrupting nearby memory. The same two-line change per loop applies with only the names changed.

subject: arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_usdhc.c: Simplify eventwait logic and remove race condition
label: unsure
evidence: The picked hunk rewrites imx9_eventwait in a commit that says 'There is a race condition when timeout and completion interrupts occur at the same time': it drops the wait loop and the DEBUGASSERT, disables and clears the wait interrupts on task cancellation, and calls nxsem_reset(&priv->waitsem, 0) after a timeout or cancellation because the semaphore 'might have been double-posted'; the same commit also moves the configwaitints call out of imx9_endwait into imx9_eventtimeout and drops the eventtimeout assumption 'Always called from the interrupt level with interrupts disabled', and those hunks are not among the picked ones. imxrt_eventwait is line for line the pre-fix imx9 code (same loop, DEBUGASSERT and trailing imxrt_configwaitints(priv, 0, 0, 0)), and imxrt_endwait, imxrt_eventtimeout and the interrupt handler match the pre-fix imx9 versions, so if the race does not depend on the platform it is present on imxrt too. From the code, a double post needs the USDHC interrupt and the watchdog callback to run at the same time, because each tests priv->waitevents before calling endwait, which clears waitevents through imxrt_configwaitints before nxsem_post; imx9 selects ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU while imxrt (Cortex-M7 or Cortex-M33) does not and still documents eventtimeout as running with interrupts disabled, and on a single CPU an extra post (possible only with nested interrupt priorities) is absorbed by the imxrt loop, which waits again while wkupevent is still 0 after imxrt_waitenable reset it. The commit message does not describe the failing sequence or say whether it needs more than one CPU, so the repository does not show whether a single-core imxrt can hit this race; a human should decide whether the imxrt loop is enough.

title: The i.MX RT uSDHC driver does not compile with DMA on and the D-cache option off, because it uses priv->rxbuffer outside the CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE guard that declares it.
summary: In August 2024 commit 23e0bf595 fixed a build error in the i.MX9 uSDHC driver: rxbuffer only exists when the data cache is in use, but the DMA preflight check and the receive setup still referred to it. The i.MX RT driver has the same code: rxbuffer is declared only under CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE, yet imxrt_dmapreflight compares the buffer with priv->rxbuffer and imxrt_dmarecvsetup uses sizeof(priv->rxbuffer) in a DEBUGASSERT that is compiled even with assertions off. A configuration with USDHC DMA (default on) and 'Use D-Cache' off (default off) therefore stops with a compile error; the shipped board configurations all enable the D-cache, so only custom configurations hit it. Carrying the fix over means using the imxrt guard CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE instead of CONFIG_ARM64_DCACHE_DISABLE, or declaring rxbuffer for every DMA build.

title: The pic32mx Ethernet driver asserts, or points the RX DMA at address 0, when no free buffer is left to replace a received one.
summary: In October 2026 the pic32mz Ethernet driver (commit 2851f1c09) stopped asserting when no free buffer is left to replace the one in a completed RX descriptor; it now drops the packet and gives the descriptor back with its current buffer, and the current pic32mz code still does this. pic32mx_rxdone still allocates the replacement with pic32mx_allocbuffer, checks it only with DEBUGASSERT, and writes PHYS_ADDR(rxbuffer) into the descriptor. If the free list is empty, a debug build stops on the assertion, and a release build hands the Ethernet DMA a descriptor that points at address 0, so the next frame is written outside the driver's buffers and that address is later treated as a driver buffer. The free list can run short on pic32mx the same way the later pic32mz commit 58b2989c6 describes, because pic32mx_bufferinit re-appends every buffer on each ifup without emptying the list. Confidence is medium because with an intact free list the pool (one buffer per descriptor plus one) should leave exactly one buffer for this allocation, so the failure depends on that buffer loss or a similar leak.

subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: Fix and enhance WWDG (Window Watchdog) support
label: missing
evidence: Two of the three at32_wwdg.c hunks do not apply: dividing WWDG_FMIN by 128 (line 65 here) and stopping the settimeout loop at wdgtb == 7 (line 552) need the STM32H7's 3-bit WDGTB field, while hardware/at32_wdg.h defines only WDGTB[1:0] at bits 8:7 with EWI at bit 9 (lines 117, 124); the at32_iwdg.c pair does not apply either, because the IWDG has no early-wakeup flag (its SR only has PVU/RVU/WVU) and that driver sets .capture = NULL. The remaining hunk, described as 'Clear the EWIF (Early Wakeup Interrupt Flag) bit in the stm32_start() function, as this bit might be set by hardware before the watchdog is actually started', meets the same logic in at32_start: it sets WDGA in WWDG_CR (line 343) without touching WWDG_SR, while at32_capture enables WWDG_CFR_EWI and the IRQ (lines 649, 652) and at32_interrupt calls the user handler whenever WWDG_SR_EWIF is set (lines 291, 302). Everything the fix uses exists on AT32: the header defines WWDG_SR_EWIF as bit 0 of AT32_WWDG_SR (line 128) and the file includes arm_internal.h, which declares modifyreg32. The clear is not tied to the H7 prescaler change: upstream's unified STM32 WWDG driver now does it unconditionally in stm32_start (common/stm32/stm32_wwdg.c line 345), including for the STM32 IP whose WDGTB[1:0] at bits 8:7 layout (common/stm32/hardware/stm32_wdg.h line 157) is the one AT32 uses. The repository does not say whether the AT32 counter itself can set EWIF before WDGA is written, so this rests on the shared register design, hence medium confidence.

title: The AT32 window watchdog is started without clearing a possibly stale early-wakeup flag (EWIF), so the early-warning handler can fire at the wrong time.
summary: In September 2025 (commit 2e85eae6b2ec) the STM32H7 window watchdog driver started clearing the EWIF flag in stm32_start before enabling the watchdog, because the flag can already be set before the watchdog is started; the unified STM32 driver now does the same for every STM32 window watchdog version. The AT32 copy, at32_start in arch/arm/src/at32/at32_wwdg.c, still enables the watchdog straight away without clearing EWIF, while at32_capture enables the early-wakeup interrupt and at32_interrupt calls the user handler whenever EWIF is set. If the flag is stale, the handler can run right away instead of shortly before expiry, and the handler is expected to reload the counter, which causes a reset if a window is configured and the counter is still above it (lines 245-248). Only the one-line flag clear needs porting (modifyreg32(AT32_WWDG_SR, WWDG_SR_EWIF, 0)); the prescaler-range hunks must not be copied because AT32 only has a 2-bit timer base field. The repository does not show whether AT32 hardware can set EWIF before activation, no in-tree board calls at32_wwdginitialize, and outside this candidate at32_getstatus (line 458) still has the pre-fix elapsed formula that the same commit corrected.

subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: Fix and enhance WWDG (Window Watchdog) support

subject: arch/arm/rp23xx: Set priority for svcall exception
label: not_applicable
evidence: The commit ('Set priority for svcall exception') adds rp23xx_prioritize_syscall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY) to up_irqinitialize; rp23xx selects ARCH_CORTEXM33 (ARMv8-M), whose up_irq_save masks interrupts by raising BASEPRI to NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY (armv8-m/irq.h line 371), so SVCall has to be placed one step above that level (armv8-m/nvicpri.h line 76) or an SVC made with interrupts masked becomes a Hard Fault, which the armv8-m arm_hardfault does not forward. kl_irq.c attaches the same SVCall and Hard Fault handlers (lines 200-201) without setting an SVCall priority, but ARCH_CHIP_KL selects ARCH_CORTEXM0, which selects ARCH_ARMV6M (arch/arm/Kconfig lines 263 and 1150). On ARMv6-M, up_irq_save disables interrupts with PRIMASK ('cpsid  i', armv6-m/irq.h line 257), which blocks SVCall whatever its priority, and the armv6-m arm_hardfault forwards an escalated 'svc 0' to arm_svcall (arm_hardfault.c lines 107-110), exactly as the comment at kl_irq.c line 196 describes. NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY is defined only in the armv7-m and armv8-m nvicpri.h headers, and none of the ARMv6-M ports (kl, nuc1xx, rp2040, samd2l2, s32k11x, common/stm32/stm32_irq_m0_v1.c) set it while their ARMv7/8-M siblings do (for example s32k14x_irq.c line 357), so the fix depends on BASEPRI masking that this core lacks.

subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: remove non-existent QSPI_CR_DMAEN references

removed: spiinfo(" EN:%1d ABORT:%1d DMAEN:%1d TCEN:%1d SSHIFT:%1d\n"

label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit ('remove non-existent QSPI_CR_DMAEN references') fixes an H7 'compilation failure when CONFIG_STM32_QSPI_DMA is enabled', but the only hunk picked out is the control-register print in qspi_dumpregs, which in stm32h7 sits inside an '#if 0' block (stm32h7/stm32_qspi.c line 501, with its '#else' at line 563 at the pinned commit, and the same layout before the fix), so it was never compiled; changing it fixes neither run-time behaviour nor the build and only edits dead logging code. The functional H7 changes (dropping the QSPI_CR_DMAEN writes in qspi_memory_dma) are not among the picked hunks. In stm32f7 the same print (lines 485 and 491) is likewise inside '#if 0' (line 477, '#else' at line 539), and here QSPI_CR_DMAEN is a real bit: the F7 header defines it as (1 << 2) with the comment 'DMA enable' (hardware/stm32_qspi.h line 82), whereas the H7 header goes straight from QSPI_CR_ABORT to QSPI_CR_TCEN, and F7 really sets it in qspi_memory_dma (line 1483). The picked hunk is therefore a logging cleanup, and even as live code the F7 print would build and report an existing bit.

subject: arch/arm/imx9: irq: replace hardcoded NVIC register lists with loops.
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The only hunk picked out for this pair changes one debug print in imx9_dumpnvic from %08x to %08lx, and the commit message says this was done "to silence warnings from the compiler for the debug dump" and that there is "No functional change for existing i.MX95-M7 builds." The matching at32 line 85 is the same INTCTRL/VECTAB print inside at32_dumpnvic, which is compiled only under CONFIG_DEBUG_IRQ_INFO (line 77) and logs through irqinfo, a macro that is a no-op unless CONFIG_DEBUG_IRQ_INFO is set (include/nuttx/debug.h). The printed values come from getreg32, a uint32_t read, and the shared arch/arm/include/types.h may make uint32_t an unsigned long while noting that sizes are 4 bytes, so %08x only draws a compiler format warning and the printed value does not change. A log-format change that only silences a warning is not a behavioural fix, so nothing was missed on at32.

summary: On 2026-08-21 the common STM32 M0 USB device driver was changed to decode value, index and len from the saved SETUP request after the optional OUT data phase, so these fields are set when stm32_ep0setup is entered a second time to finish an OUT control transfer; the same change fixed Clang builds that treat maybe-uninitialized diagnostics as errors. With a compliant host this most likely changes nothing at run time, because SET_DESCRIPTOR, the only standard OUT request with data, is handed to the class driver without using them; a request with an unexpected data phase may be accepted or stalled at random, and the file would hit the same Clang error. The fix can be copied over unchanged.

title: The pic32mx Ethernet driver takes received frames out of ring order and loses responses that are waiting for a free TX descriptor.
summary: On 2026-10-10 the pic32mz Ethernet driver fixed its RX path: it now takes RX descriptors in ring order using a ring index, stops receiving while a response waits for a free TX descriptor (and txavail no longer polls over that response), and also processes RX descriptors on overflow and buffer-not-available events. The pic32mx driver, which has the same structure, still scans its RX descriptor ring from index 0 in pic32mx_rxdesc, keeps receiving after pic32mx_response has marked a response as pending and then frees that response's buffer, and reacts only to RXDONE. Under load this can deliver frames out of order and lose responses, and with assertions enabled pic32mx_transmit asserts when txdone sends the pending packet with a NULL buffer. The patch has to be adapted rather than copied: pic32mx never decrements BUFCNT in its RX path, so the BUFCDEC reordering does not carry over and the effect of the overflow-event hunk on pic32mx is not shown by the code, and nothing here was tested on PIC32MX hardware.

title: The RA4 serial error interrupt handler never clears its ICU IELSR.IR flag, the bug the RA8M1 copy fixed because it livelocked the system on receive errors.
summary: On 2026-10-06 commit 5c3c2cbf fixed the RA8M1 serial driver's up_erinterrupt() to call ra_clear_ir(irq), after hardware testing showed that leaving the ICU IELSR.IR flag set made the NVIC re-enter the handler and livelocked the board on any receive error. The RA4 driver, whose ra_serial.c has the same handler structure, still has the old handler at the pinned commit: up_erinterrupt() only saves and clears the SSR error bits, while its RX and TX handlers already call ra_clear_ir(irq). Because RA4 routes SCIn_ERI through the same IELSR mechanism and has the same ra_clear_ir() helper, a parity, framing or overrun error on an RA4 UART would most likely leave the error interrupt pending and hang the system. Adding ra_clear_ir(irq) at the top of the handler carries over directly; the RA8M1 receive-drain part relies on SCI_B behaviour that the repository does not document for the RA4M1 SCI, so whether it is also needed is uncertain. None of this has been confirmed on RA4 hardware.

evidence: The commit message says 'Serial IFLOW build error fixed for risc-v based Espressif devices': in the common Espressif driver (arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif) esp_rxflowcontrol called esp_lowputc_set_iflow() and UART_RX_FIFO_SIZE, neither of which that driver defines (its esp_lowputc.h/.c at the fix's parent have no set_iflow function), so the hunks replace them with the HAL call uart_hal_set_hw_flow_ctrl(priv->hal, ...). subject: esp32/ble: fix saving/restoring the interrupt status flags
label: missing
evidence: The ESP32 commit replaces the single saved flag used by the BLE controller callbacks interrupt_disable()/interrupt_restore() with a list of saved flags because 'calling nested enter_critical_section would overwrite this global variable that was storing the previous flag and, when leaving the last critical section, the restored status would be different from the one expected'. esp32c3-legacy/esp32c3_ble_adapter.c still has exactly the pre-fix code: one static irqstate_t g_inter_flags, interrupt_disable() doing g_inter_flags = enter_critical_section(), interrupt_restore() doing leave_critical_section(g_inter_flags), and both are handed to the BLE controller library through the same ._interrupt_disable/._interrupt_restore callback slots as on ESP32. The fix uses only generic NuttX code (sq_queue lists, or the nesting counter g_ble_int_count that ESP32 uses today) and no chip feature, and the legacy adapter has no nesting guard of any kind, while the ESP32 and ESP32-S3 adapters and the newer ESP32-C3 adapter arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c all keep one. The legacy OSI table also uses the same OSI_VERSION 0x00010006 as the ESP32-S3 adapter that received the same fix (commit 6521bdfa1). Confidence is medium because whether the binary legacy ESP32-C3 controller library really nests these calls cannot be seen in the repository.
title: The legacy ESP32-C3 BLE adapter keeps the saved interrupt state of BLE critical sections in one global variable, so a nested call loses the outer state.
summary: On 2023-11-10 the ESP32 BLE adapter (commit 606190d9b) stopped saving the interrupt state of the controller's interrupt_disable/interrupt_restore callbacks in a single global, because a nested call overwrote the outer saved state; the ESP32, ESP32-S3 and newer ESP32-C3 adapters all still guard against nesting today, now with a nesting counter. The legacy ESP32-C3 adapter still writes every enter_critical_section() result into the one static g_inter_flags and restores that value on every interrupt_restore. If the controller library nests these calls, the outermost interrupt_restore restores the already-disabled state, so interrupts can stay disabled after the BLE critical section ends. The repository cannot show whether the binary legacy ESP32-C3 controller library actually nests these calls; the case rests on the identical callback code and interface and on the fixes made to the sibling adapters.
same_problem_note: Same saved-interrupt-state global in esp32c3_ble_adapter.c as nuttx-180: the same fix was made in the ESP32-S3 BLE adapter on 2023-10-05 and in the ESP32 adapter on 2023-11-10.

subject: arch/arm/imxrt: LPUART DMA fixes
label: missing
evidence: The listed hunk makes imxrt_dma_txcallback() count dmatx.nlength as sent only when CONFIG_IMXRT_EDMA_NTCD > 1 (the same commit also stops imxrt_dma_send() from queuing the wrapped second segment otherwise), because, in the commit message's words, 'Without in-memory TCDs, submitting the second segment overwrites the active hardware descriptor and incorrectly advances the serial buffer past unsent data.' s32k1xx_dma_txcallback() still sets nbytes = length + nlength unconditionally (line 1744), and s32k1xx_dma_send() still calls s32k1xx_dmach_xfrsetup() a second time for the wrapped part whenever dmatx.nbuffer is set (lines 1826-1831), with no check of CONFIG_S32K1XX_EDMA_NTCD. That option defaults to 0 (Kconfig line 580), and in that build s32k1xx_dmach_xfrsetup() programs the channel TCD registers directly and returns -EBUSY when the TCD CSR is non-zero and not DONE (s32k1xx_edma.c lines 1046-1048), which holds after the first segment set DREQ and INTMAJOR, so the second segment is never queued (dma_send ignores the return value) while uart_xmitchars_done() still moves the tail by nbytes (serial_dma.c line 185), dropping the wrapped bytes unsent. title: S32K1xx LPUART TX DMA marks the wrapped part of the TX buffer as sent although it was never transmitted when scatter/gather descriptors are not configured.
summary: In September 2026 (commit 6b0f85b7) the i.MX RT LPUART driver was changed to queue and count the wrapped second part of the TX ring buffer only when CONFIG_IMXRT_EDMA_NTCD > 1, that is, only when scatter/gather descriptors exist. The S32K1xx LPUART driver has the same TX DMA code: it always tries to queue the second part and its completion callback always reports both parts as sent. With the default CONFIG_S32K1XX_EDMA_NTCD=0 the eDMA driver refuses the second part with -EBUSY, so only the first part is transmitted, yet the serial layer frees both, and any write whose data wraps around the end of the TX buffer silently loses the wrapped bytes. This only affects builds that enable LPUART TX DMA (CONFIG_LPUARTn_TXDMA), which no in-tree s32k1xx defconfig does. The fix is the same NTCD guard in s32k1xx_dma_txcallback() and s32k1xx_dma_send(), plus restarting the next transfer from the callback so the remaining bytes do not wait for the next write.

title: S32K1xx LPSPI DMA exchange counts 4 bytes per 16-bit word, so 9-16-bit transfers overrun the caller's buffers.
summary: In October 2024 the i.MX9 LPSPI driver fixed its DMA exchange for 9-16-bit words: it now counts 2 bytes per word instead of 4 and programs the DMA with the number of words instead of that byte count. The S32K1xx LPSPI DMA exchange is the same older code: it still counts 4 bytes per word and uses that count as the number of 16-bit DMA items, while the DMA reads and writes the caller's buffers directly. A 9-16-bit SPI exchange on a DMA-enabled LPSPI therefore clocks out four times as many frames, reads past the end of the TX buffer and writes past the end of the RX buffer, corrupting memory. The same three-line change applies here unchanged (the byte count plus the two config.iter lines); changing only the byte count would still leave the DMA moving twice the requested words.

title: S32K3xx LPSPI DMA exchange counts 4 bytes per 16-bit word, so 9-16-bit transfers overrun the caller's buffers.
summary: In October 2024 the i.MX9 LPSPI driver fixed its DMA exchange for 9-16-bit words: it now counts 2 bytes per word instead of 4 and programs the DMA with the number of words. The S32K3xx LPSPI DMA exchange still has the older code: it counts 4 bytes per word and uses that count as the number of 16-bit DMA items on the caller's buffers, so a 9-16-bit exchange clocks four times as many frames and reads and writes past the ends of the TX and RX buffers. Because the DMA threshold option cannot be enabled on this chip, every exchange on a DMA-enabled LPSPI goes this way. The port needs care: the in-tree FS26 safety chip driver uses 32-bit frames on a DMA-enabled LPSPI3 (mr-canhubk3 'net' defconfig), so the change should be limited to 9-16-bit frames rather than copied as is; whether the current 32-bit path is itself correct cannot be decided from the code.

subject: arch/xtensa/esp32: Fix buffer overflow in SPI poll exchange
label: missing
evidence: The hunks bound each memcpy() in esp32_spi_poll_exchange() by the bytes still left in the transfer and advance tp/rp by that amount, because, in the commit message's words, 'When an SPI transaction involved a data length not aligned to 4 bytes ... the driver forced a 4-byte memory transfer. This caused out-of-bounds reads and writes, leading to stack smashing and fatal CPU exceptions'. esp32c3_spi_poll_exchange() in esp32c3-legacy is the same pre-fix function: total_bytes = nwords * (priv->nbits / 8) (line 919), chunks of MIN(SPI_MAX_BUF_SIZE, bytes_remaining) (line 931), and in both loops it copies a full sizeof(uint32_t) from tp (line 943) and into rp (line 1006) and steps by sizeof(uintptr_t) (lines 945, 1008) whatever transfer_size is. So any exchange whose byte count is not a multiple of 4 reads up to 3 bytes past the TX buffer and writes up to 3 bytes past the caller's RX buffer. The function handles every exchange when CONFIG_ESP32C3_SPI2_DMA is off (its default) and the short ones at or below the DMA threshold when it is on (lines 1053-1060), and nothing else limits the copies; the RX loop already sits inside if (rp != NULL) (line 989), so the NULL-check part of the fix is redundant here but the chunk limits port with no renaming.
title: ESP32-C3 (legacy) SPI polling exchange copies whole 4-byte words past the end of buffers whose length is not a multiple of 4.
summary: In February 2026 the ESP32 SPI driver fixed esp32_spi_poll_exchange() so that each memcpy() copies only the bytes left in the transfer instead of always 4, because 1-byte and other unaligned transfers were reading and writing past the caller's buffers and smashing the stack. The ESP32-C3 legacy driver's esp32c3_spi_poll_exchange() is the same code and still copies 4 bytes per data register in both the transmit and receive loops. Any polled exchange whose length is not a multiple of 4 bytes (every such exchange without SPI DMA, and the short ones with it) writes up to 3 bytes past the end of the receive buffer and reads up to 3 bytes past the transmit buffer, which can corrupt the stack or neighbouring data. The fix ports unchanged: take the chunk as the smaller of 4 and the bytes left, and use it for both copies and pointer steps.

title: AT32 PWM stop does not clear the channel compare registers, so a channel can come back with its old duty after a stop.
summary: In February 2024 the STM32 PWM driver started zeroing the four channel compare registers (CCR1-CCR4) in pwm_stop(), because after a STOP in multichannel mode a channel was still outputting; the same lines are now also in the STM32F7, H7 and H5 drivers. The AT32 PWM driver, which was copied from the STM32 driver, still only stops the counter and disables the outputs, leaving the old duty values in place. Because a later start rewrites the duty only of the channels it lists but re-enables every configured output, a channel that is not listed in the next start comes back with its previous duty instead of staying off. The fix ports by renaming the register offsets to AT32_GTIM_CCRx_OFFSET; the commit does not explain the exact STOP symptom, so the restart case above is the effect that can be confirmed from the code.

subject: rp2040/gpio: Fix debug assertion for interrupts.
label: not_applicable
evidence: The commit message says "The previous interrupt implementation allowed only one single interrupt mode to be selected. The debug assertion is now updated to allow the entire range of possible interrupt combinations (a 4-bit field), up to 0xf." It follows the earlier RP2040 change ac583fc58 ("Allow simultaneous selection of multiple interrupt modes"), which turned the RP2040 modes into bit flags (RP2040_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH is now 0x8) and enables them with ((uint8_t)g_gpio_irq_modes[gpio] & 0xf) << ((gpio % 8) * 4), so the old bound rejected valid combinations. In arch/arm/src/rp23xx the modes are still plain indices 0..3 (RP23XX_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH is 3), and rp23xx_gpio_enable_irq() sets exactly one bit with 0x1 << ((gpio % 8) * 4 + g_gpio_irq_modes[gpio]). With that encoding, intrmode <= RP23XX_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH in rp23xx_gpio_irq_attach() is the correct bound, and widening it to 0xf would let values 4..15 shift into the next pin's enable bits. The multi-mode change that the fix depends on was never ported to rp23xx, so the fix does not apply.

subject: arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR
label: missing

The AT32 DMA setup only has DEBUGASSERT(ntransfers < 65536), the same check as the STM32 IPv1 DMAMUX driver (common/stm32/stm32_dma_m3m4_v1_8ch_dmamux.c line 735), and then writes ntransfers into the CNDTR register, while spi_dmarxwait() loops on nxsem_wait_uninterruptible() until the DMA callback sets rxresult, with no timeout. title: The AT32 SPI DMA exchange does not split requests larger than the 16-bit DMA transfer count and does not shrink nwords when the copy is clipped to the driver buffer.
summary: Upstream commit 8302295dd018 (2026-05-15) changed the STM32 SPI driver to run DMA exchanges in chunks of at most 65535 words and to shrink nwords when the copy into the driver's own DMA buffer is clipped to buflen. The AT32 copy in at32_spi.c still hands the full nwords to spi_dmarxsetup()/spi_dmatxsetup() and on to at32_dmasetup(), whose only guard is a debug assertion before the value is written into the CNDTR register, and it then waits for the DMA callback with no timeout. An exchange of 65536 words or more therefore trips the assertion in debug builds and otherwise programs a truncated count, which per the STM32 commit hangs the caller (for an exact 64 Ki-word transfer) or silently exchanges fewer words than requested. When an in-driver DMA buffer is configured and the request is larger than it, the DMA is still programmed with the unclipped nwords and can run past that buffer. The fix has to be adapted so that each chunk keeps the SPIEN disable/enable steps that the AT32 version performs around the DMA setup.

title: The STM32L4 SPI DMA exchange puts the whole request into the 16-bit DMA CNDTR count without splitting it, so exchanges of 65536 or more words get a truncated count.
summary: In May 2026 apache/nuttx commit 8302295dd0 changed the STM32 (F1/F2/F3/F4/G4/L1) SPI driver to split DMA exchanges into chunks of at most 65535 words, because the DMA count register is 16 bits wide and an exact 64 KiB exchange left the caller blocked in spi_dmarxwait(). The STM32L4 SPI driver still sets up one DMA transfer with the caller's full nwords, and the L4 DMA driver writes that value into CNDTR, whose count field is 16 bits, with only a debug assertion as a guard. If not fixed, an exchange of 65536 or more words would move only the low 16 bits' worth of data, and with exactly 65536 words the commit reports a hang. At the pinned commit, however, the Kconfig offers no way to enable SPI DMA on STM32L4, so the problem is latent; a human should confirm whether that missing switch is intended before deciding how much the port matters.

title: The GD32VW55x SPI DMA exchange puts the whole request into a 16-bit DMA count, so exchanges of 65536 or more words are silently truncated.
summary: In May 2026 apache/nuttx commit 8302295dd0 made the STM32 SPI driver split DMA exchanges into chunks of at most 65535 words, because the DMA transfer count is 16 bits wide and an exact 64 KiB exchange left the caller blocked in spi_dmarxwait(). The fix has to be rewritten for gd32_dma_setup() (a loop over chunks that advances the buffer pointers), since this driver has no bounce buffer; the fix commit notes that 'Single-descriptor transfers (every in-tree caller today) are byte-for-byte identical', so the problem shows only for exchanges of 65536 or more words.

subject: arch/arm/rp23xx: Fix IRQ prioritize
label: missing
evidence: The commit message says it "Fixes the reg addresses that were copied from armv6 rp2040 to the actual armv8 spec", but only the second hunk changes behaviour: the first hunk swaps ARMV6M_NVIC_IPR(irq >> 2) for NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY(irq), which give the same address (0xe000e400 + 4*(irq >> 2) by armv6-m/nvic.h and armv8-m/nvic.h), so it is only a rename that ARMv6-M code does not need, while the second hunk moves the PendSV and SysTick writes from SHPR2 (0xe000ed1c) to NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY (0xe000ed20, "System handler 12-15 priority register") with the same shift values 16 and 24. In nuc1xx up_prioritize_irq() (nuc_irq.c 347-356, built with CONFIG_ARCH_IRQPRIO, which this chip can enable because ARCH_CHIP_NUC1XX selects ARCH_CORTEXM0 and that selects ARCH_HAVE_IRQPRIO) the PendSV and SysTick branches are the same pre-fix lines, still writing ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR2 with SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_14_SHIFT / SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_15_SHIFT. The armv6-m/nvic.h that nuc_irq.c includes as "nvic.h" puts PendSV (bits 16-23) and SysTick (bits 24-31) in System handler priority register 3 at offset 0x0020 and gives SHPR2 only the SVCall field in bits 24-31, and nuc_timerisr.c itself sets the SysTick priority through ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3. So the register error is not specific to ARMv8: a SysTick request rewrites the SVCall priority, which the function comment says must not be modified, and neither the PendSV nor the SysTick priority changes; the other ARMv6-M copies (rp2040, kl, samd2l2) carry the same lines, so none shows a different handling.

title: nuc1xx up_prioritize_irq() writes the PendSV and SysTick priorities into SHPR2 instead of SHPR3, so a SysTick request changes the SVCall priority instead.
summary: On 2025-04-16 commit 8ac09bcf fixed rp23xx up_prioritize_irq() so that PendSV and SysTick priorities go to System Handler Priority Register 3 (0xe000ed20) instead of SHPR2 (0xe000ed1c); that code had been copied from the ARMv6-M rp2040 driver. The nuc1xx copy still uses ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR2 with the SHPR3 field shifts, although its own armv6-m header places PendSV and SysTick in SHPR3 and SVCall in SHPR2 bits 24-31, and its timer code already uses SHPR3 for SysTick. With CONFIG_ARCH_IRQPRIO enabled, asking for a new SysTick priority silently changes the SVCall priority, asking for a new PendSV priority writes unused SHPR2 bits, and in both cases the requested priority never takes effect although the function returns OK. Only the register part of the fix applies (use ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3 in both branches); the rename to ARMv8-M macro names does not, and nothing in arch/arm/src/nuc1xx or arch/arm/src/armv6-m calls this function, so the problem only shows when board or application code reprioritizes PendSV or SysTick.

subject: arch/mips/pic32mz: fix the Ethernet D-Cache coherency.
label: not_applicable
evidence: The commit message ties both changes to the PIC32MZ data cache: VIRT_ADDR() mapped buffers to KSEG1 although g_buffers "is linked in KSEG0 when the data memory is cached", and an RX buffer "may still have dirty D-Cache lines", so the fix takes the segment from g_buffers and adds pic32mz_rxbuffer(), which calls up_invalidate_dcache() before a buffer is given to the DMA. The repository gives PIC32MX no data cache: the PIC32MZ chip entries select MIPS32_HAVE_DCACHE, ARCH_CHIP_PIC32MX7 (like every PIC32MX family) selects only ARCH_MIPS_M4K, "Use D-Cache" (MIPS32_DCACHE) depends on MIPS32_HAVE_DCACHE, ARCH_DCACHE is a hidden option selected only by MIPS32_DCACHE and JZ4780, so on PIC32MX up_invalidate_dcache() is the empty macro of include/nuttx/cache.h, and mips_cache.S is built only by pic32mz/Make.defs. pic32mx_ethernet.c also has no cache maintenance anywhere and keeps its buffers in pd_buffers inside the static g_ethdrvr (there is no g_buffers), and all 19 linker scripts under boards/mips/pic32mx place .bss in KSEG1 data memory (0xa0000200), so the buffers already live in the segment that VIRT_ADDR() at line 273 converts to and are never reached through two aliases. The fix therefore depends on cached data memory, which the PIC32MX port does not have.

label: missing

At the pinned commit the serial upper half (drivers/serial/serial.c, serial_dma.c) calls dmatxavail only from write, drain and echo paths, uart_xmitchars_done and uart_datasent only advance the tail and wake waiters, and s32k1xx_dma_txint does nothing, so bytes queued while a transfer is running stay in the buffer until a later write. The port must be adapted: s32k1xx_edma.c has no dmach_idle function, and s32k1xx_dmaterminate invokes the callback (line 494) before setting S32K1XX_DMA_IDLE (line 499), the ordering s32k3xx changed in the companion commit 7f0643de6 ('edma clear state before callback add idle check'), so an idle check made inside the callback needs that change as well.
title: s32k1xx LPUART TX DMA leaves bytes that were queued during a running transfer unsent until the next write.
summary: On 2023-12-05 s32k3xx_serial.c dropped its TX DMA semaphore and made the DMA completion callback restart DMA whenever the transmit buffer still holds data, fixing stuttering output caused by the earlier switch to nxsem_trywait. s32k1xx_serial.c received that same trywait switch in November 2023 but still has the old code: its completion callback only posts txdmasem, and s32k1xx_dma_txavailable silently skips sending when the trywait fails. Data written while a TX DMA transfer is in flight therefore stays in the transmit buffer until some later write, drain or echo calls dmatxavail again, so serial or console output can stall or arrive in bursts. Porting also needs the matching eDMA change: an idle-check function and marking the channel idle before the callback runs in s32k1xx_dmaterminate.

subject: arch/risc-v/rp23xx-rv: Fix PWM frequency and duty cycle calculation.

removed: pwminfo("PWM%d freq %ld max %ld\n", priv->num, priv->frequency, max_freq);

label: missing
evidence: The commit message says it fixed "three bugs" in the rp23xx-rv PWM driver, "mirroring the fix previously applied to the ARM variant": setup_period's divisor "used integer arithmetic that caused overflow and loss of precision", setup_pulse's compare "was incorrectly scaled by TOP instead of 65535, producing wrong duty cycles", and pwm_start still used info[0].duty after commit 4df80e19 removed PWM_MULTICHAN. arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_pwm.c still has all three pre-fix pieces with only the prefix changed: pwm_start reads info[0].duty in the CONFIG_PWM_NCHANNELS != 2 branch (lines 362-364), setup_period computes top = 0xffff / (frequency / max_freq) and divisor = 16 * max_freq / frequency with no range clamp (lines 471-503), and setup_pulse computes 0xffff * duty / top (lines 535-538), while arch/arm/src/rp23xx/rp23xx_pwm.c and the rp23xx-rv driver now use info->channels[0].duty, a clamped div16 and duty * (top + 1) / 65535. Everything the fix relies on exists for rp2040: struct pwm_info_s now only has channels[CONFIG_PWM_NCHANNELS] (include/nuttx/timers/pwm.h line 218) and PWM_NCHANNELS defaults to 1 (drivers/timers/Kconfig lines 90-92), so the single-channel rp2040 build fails, and hardware/rp2040_pwm.h defines the same 8-bit INT and 4-bit FRAC divider fields (lines 90-93) that the 0x10..0xFFF clamp targets. From the code itself, whenever top is reduced below 0xffff the old compare 0xffff * duty / top is scaled up instead of down, so it no longer matches the requested duty and for most duty values exceeds top (in the two-channel sum it then spills into the B field), and the old divisor can fall below 0x10 (e.g. 3000 Hz at 125 MHz gives 16 * 1907 / 3000 = 10) or exceed 0xFFF (1 Hz gives 30512); rp2040 has no other code that handles this.
title: The rp2040 PWM driver still has the old divider and duty-cycle formulas and the removed info[0].duty field access that were fixed in both rp23xx PWM drivers.
summary: The ARM rp23xx PWM driver was fixed on 2026-05-25 (commit 53ef7c063) and the RISC-V rp23xx-rv copy on 2026-06-24 (commit 970f2f22): the clock divider is now a clamped 8.4 fixed-point value, the compare value is duty * (top + 1) / 65535 clamped to top, and pwm_start reads info->channels[0].duty. arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_pwm.c still has the identical old code in pwm_start, setup_period and setup_pulse. If it is not fixed, a single-channel build (PWM_NCHANNELS=1, the Kconfig default) does not compile because struct pwm_info_s has no duty member, and at run time any frequency that forces top below 0xffff gives a wrongly scaled compare value (wrong duty cycle, for most duties above top, and in two-channel mode corrupting channel B), while the divider can be written outside the 0x10..0xFFF range. The patch can be carried over by renaming the rp23xx identifiers to rp2040 ones; this is based on reading the code only, not on hardware tests.
same_problem_note: Same three pre-fix places in rp2040_pwm.c as nuttx-143: the same PWM fix was made in the rp23xx driver on 2026-05-25 and in its RISC-V copy on 2026-06-24.

title: The cxd56 SPI driver waits for DMA completion with no timeout, so a DMA transfer that never finishes hangs the caller forever.
summary: On 2026-10-13 the rp23xx SPI driver (ARM and RISC-V ports) changed spi_dmatrxwait() to wait for the TX and RX DMA completions with nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() and a timeout derived from the transfer size and SPI clock, and on timeout to stop both DMA channels, reset the semaphore and drain the RX FIFO. subject: Fix Serial APB Clock Sources
label: missing

title: The STM32WL5 serial driver computes the LPUART1 baud divisor from PCLK2, although LPUART1 is clocked from APB1 (PCLK1).
summary: On 2024-11-07 the STM32H5 serial driver fixed LPUART1 (and three USARTs) whose apbclock had been left at the default PCLK2 instead of the clock of the bus the port is on. The STM32WL5 serial driver still sets LPUART1's apbclock to STM32_PCLK2_FREQUENCY and uses it for the baud divisor, while its own clock-enable code, RCC header and early console code all treat LPUART1 as an APB1/PCLK1 peripheral. On a board whose APB1 and APB2 prescalers differ, the serial driver would program a wrong LPUART1 baud rate that also disagrees with what the early console set up. The change has to be adapted: on WL5 the value should be STM32_PCLK1_FREQUENCY, not PCLK3. The only in-tree board runs PCLK1 and PCLK2 at the same 48 MHz, so no in-tree configuration shows the error today.

title: The ESP32-C3 BLE adapter's esp_update_time() can leave tv_nsec at one second or more, so timed BLE message-queue sends and receives fail with EINVAL.
summary: On 2024-10-07, commit b3727f67bee3 rewrote esp_update_time() in the ESP32, ESP32-S3 and legacy ESP32-C3 BLE and Wi-Fi adapters to use clock_ticks2time() and clock_timespec_add(), which carry nanoseconds above one second into tv_sec. The newer ESP32-C3 BLE adapter (arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c) still has the old body, even though esp_wifi_adapter.c in the same directory has the fixed one. Whenever the current time's nanoseconds plus the timeout's fraction of a second reach one second, file_mq_timedsend() and file_mq_timedreceive() reject the deadline with -EINVAL, so a timed BLE queue send fails and a timed receive returns at once instead of waiting. This is the same failure the commit reports for Wi-Fi scanning, and the two-line fix can be copied as is.

subject: arm: sama5: sam_ehci: fix transfer cancellation process.
label: missing
evidence: The sama5 commit 'arm: sama5: sam_ehci: fix transfer cancellation process.' says 'The logic of the conditional expression that determines whether the QH is a target QH or not is reversed in the process of canceling a transfer in INPROGRESS state' and that therefore 'the QH in INPROGRESS state is not released and subsequent communication is not successful'; the listed hunk flips sam_qh_cancel()'s test to 'if (qh->epinfo != epinfo)' (sam_ehci.c line 2724). imxrt_ehci.c line 3149 is in imxrt_qh_cancel(), the same imxrt_qh_foreach() callback that imxrt_cancel() passes at line 4900, and it still returns OK under the comment 'No... keep looking' when qh->epinfo == epinfo, so it skips the QH being cancelled and would unlink and free a non-matching one instead. The companion test that the same commit flipped in sam_cancel() (sam_ehci.c line 4446) is also still pre-fix here, written with the per-controller head: 'if (qh && qh != priv->asynchead)' at line 4846 claims success without searching whenever the asynchronous queue is not empty. Nothing the fix relies on is missing: QHs record their epinfo (line 1894), imxrt_qh_cancel() is built under CONFIG_USBHOST_ASYNCH (line 3131), which IMXRT_USBOTG1 selects (arch/arm/src/imxrt/Kconfig line 571), and the change is plain C logic with no register dependence.
title: imxrt EHCI transfer cancellation tests for the target QH the wrong way round, so a cancelled in-progress transfer is never removed from the schedule.
summary: On 2024-01-20 commit bca8df7d fixed two reversed tests in sama5's EHCI transfer cancellation: sam_qh_cancel() now skips QHs that belong to other endpoints, and sam_cancel() skips the search only when the asynchronous queue is empty. imxrt_ehci.c has the same cancellation code and still has both pre-fix tests: imxrt_qh_cancel() treats the matching QH as 'keep looking' (line 3149), and imxrt_cancel() reports success without searching whenever the queue holds any QH (line 4846). As the sama5 commit message describes, cancelling a bulk or control transfer that is still in progress then leaves its QH linked in the schedule, and later communication with the device fails (the sama5 fix was checked with the CDC-ACM driver and the cu command). The listed hunk is a one-operator change, but the companion test at line 4846 must be flipped as well (with priv->asynchead in place of &g_asynchead) for the search to run at all.

subject: risc-v/bl808, sg2000: Configure MMU to cache Kernel Text, Data and Heap (T-Head C906)
label: not_applicable
evidence: The hunks OR MMU_THEAD_PMA_FLAGS into the kernel text, data and page-pool mappings of bl808_kernel_mappings() and sg2000_kernel_mappings(); the commit message says it configures 'the BL808 and SG2000 MMU (inside T-Head C906) to cache the the Kernel Text, Data and Heap', and the flag is built from PTE bits 60-62 that those files define under '/* T-Head C906 MMU Extensions */' (bl808_mm_init.c lines 45-61). In arch/risc-v/Kconfig, ARCH_CHIP_BL808 and ARCH_CHIP_SG2000 select ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD (lines 472 and 518), and the shared riscv_mmu.h defines the T-Head 'Shareable, Bufferable, Cacheable' PTE bits only under '#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD' (lines 51-53). ARCH_CHIP_JH7110 (line 440) does not select ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD, and jh7110_mm_init.c defines no T-Head bits at all: it even maps its I/O region with the plain MMU_IO_FLAGS (line 240), where bl808 and sg2000 need a T-Head strong-order variant. The jh7110 lines 245, 248 and 258 are textually the pre-fix code, but the vendor-specific PTE attributes the fix adds belong to the T-Head MMU extension, which this chip is not configured with.

subject: risc-v/bl808, sg2000: Configure MMU to cache Kernel Text, Data and Heap (T-Head C906)
label: not_applicable

These PTE bits are a vendor extension: riscv_mmu.h defines the T-Head bits only under CONFIG_ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD, and in arch/risc-v/Kconfig that option is selected by ARCH_CHIP_BL808 and ARCH_CHIP_SG2000 but not by ARCH_CHIP_QEMU_RV. qemu_rv_mm_init.c defines no T-Head flags, its map_region() takes a uint32_t mmuflags (the BL808 copy takes uint64_t), and QEMU RV can also be built as SV32 (ARCH_CHIP_QEMU_RV32), where bits 60-63 do not exist. The unchanged map_region()/mmu_ln_map_region() calls in qemu_rv_kernel_mappings() are therefore the generic RISC-V mapping for a core without the T-Head MMU extension, not a missed fix.

subject: arch/nrf91: fix compilation for SPI
label: missing
evidence: The nrf91 commit "fix compilation for SPI" ("remove references to unsupported SPI freq and SPI4 which is not supported") drops the SPIM4 exception from the >8 MHz limit in setfrequency because NRF91_SPIM4_BASE does not exist on that chip. nrf53_spi_setfrequency() line 787 has the same pre-fix check; on the nRF5340 application core it is correct and needed (NRF53_SPIM4_BASE is defined in nrf53_memorymap_cpuapp.h, the driver has a g_spi4dev instance, SPIM_FREQUENCY_16MBPS/32MBPS exist), so the nrf91 deletion itself must not be copied. But the same driver also builds for the network core: Kconfig offers NRF53_SPI0_MASTER outside "if NRF53_HAVE_SPI1234" (selected only by NRF53_APPCORE), nrf53_memorymap.h then includes nrf53_memorymap_cpunet.h, which defines only NRF53_SPIM0_BASE, and line 787 is under no #ifdef (the only other SPIM4 use, line 394, is inside CONFIG_NRF53_SPI4_MASTER). A net-core build with SPI0 enabled would therefore hit the same undefined SPIM4-base compile error the nrf91 commit fixed; no in-tree *_cpunet defconfig enables SPI, so it is latent, and the adapted fix is a guard (for example on CONFIG_NRF53_SPI4_MASTER) rather than deleting the check.
impact_note: It is only a compile failure, and only for a network-core configuration with SPI0 enabled, which no in-tree board config uses; application-core builds compile and run unchanged.
title: The nRF53 SPI driver uses NRF53_SPIM4_BASE unconditionally, so a network-core build with SPI0 enabled fails to compile.
summary: In March 2024 the nrf91 SPI driver was fixed to build by removing the SPIM4 exception from the >8 MHz frequency limit, because nRF91 has no SPIM4. The nrf53 copy still has the same check at line 787 in nrf53_spi_setfrequency(); it is correct on the nRF5340 application core, which has SPIM4, but the network-core memory map defines only SPIM0 while Kconfig still lets SPI0 be enabled there. In that configuration the driver would fail to compile on an undefined NRF53_SPIM4_BASE, the same error nrf91 had. No in-tree network-core board config enables SPI, so the problem is latent, and the fix has to be a conditional guard rather than the nrf91 deletion. This comes from reading Kconfig and headers only; no network-core build was tried.

subject: arch/arm/imxrt: Fix EDMA_ALIGN for Cortex-M33 in imxrt_edma_ver2.c
label: fixed_differently
evidence: The commit message calls it a "Small fix to compile imxrt_edma_ver2.c correctly also for M33": imxrt/chip.h defines ARMV8M_DCACHE_LINESIZE under CONFIG_ARCH_CORTEXM33 and ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE only in the #else branch, so the old "EDMA_ALIGN ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE" did not build for an i.MX RT M33. imx9_edma.c line 89 has the same pre-fix define, and the arm imx9 port can also target a Cortex-M33 (ARCH_CHIP_IMX93_M33 selects ARCH_CORTEXM33), but imx9/chip.h, which imx9_edma.c includes, defines ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE as 32 with no core condition. So on both imx9 cores EDMA_ALIGN resolves to 32 bytes, the same value the imxrt fix yields on M33, and the build error does not occur; nothing under imx9 defines ARMV8M_DCACHE_LINESIZE, so copying the imxrt change verbatim would instead break the i.MX93 M33 build. The difference lies only in how the chip header is written, so imx9 already avoids the problem another way.

subject: arch/arm/stm32{|f7}/socketcan: fix debugassert for extid frames
label: missing
evidence: The stm32/stm32f7 commit says "fix debugassert for extid frames, we have to remove CAN_EFF_FLAG bit from the expression": inside "if (frame->can_id & CAN_EFF_FLAG)" the ID always carries CAN_EFF_FLAG (0x80000000 in include/nuttx/can.h), so "frame->can_id < (1 << 29)" can never hold and the assertion fires on every extended-ID frame when debug assertions are enabled. at32can_transmit() in at32_can_sock.c has exactly the same branch and assertion at line 892, followed by the same bxCAN-style ID write (ID shifted by CAN_TMI_TMEID_SHIFT plus the ID-type bit), and nothing chip-specific is involved: CAN_EFF_FLAG is already used on line 890 and the corrected expression needs nothing else. Separately, the same CONFIG_NET_CAN_EXTID block uses CAN_TIR_EXID_MASK on line 889, which no header reachable from at32 defines (only STM32 hardware headers do), and the only in-tree at32 socket config (at32f437-mini can_socket) does not enable NET_CAN_EXTID, so this path does not build today and the bug is masked. Once extended-ID support is made to build on at32, the wrong assertion would trip on the first extended frame; the STM32 one-line change can be copied unchanged.
impact_note: DEBUGASSERT is only active in debug-assertion builds, and on at32 the extended-ID block currently does not compile (line 889 uses an STM32-only macro), so no working build reaches this line today.
title: The at32 SocketCAN transmit path asserts that an extended CAN ID, still carrying the EFF flag, is below 2^29, which always fails for extended frames.
summary: In October 2024 the stm32 and stm32f7 SocketCAN drivers changed the extended-ID assertion to drop CAN_EFF_FLAG before comparing against 2^29. The at32 copy still asserts frame->can_id < (1 << 29) inside the branch that requires CAN_EFF_FLAG, so with debug assertions on, sending any extended-ID frame would stop the system. Right now this is masked because the same CONFIG_NET_CAN_EXTID block also uses CAN_TIR_EXID_MASK, which at32 does not define, so extended-ID support does not build on at32; whoever fixes that build error will hit the assertion next. The STM32 one-line change applies unchanged.

subject: arch/arm/src/samv7/sam_mcan.c: fix potential false debug assertions
label: missing
evidence: The samv7 commit explains that the TX FIFO can be "not full but the semaphore is not yet incremented because the driver didn't handle the interrupt", which "leads to the debug assertion", and that "mcan_buffer_reserve function will take care of fixing the semaphore value if it doesn't match with the FIFO"; it therefore drops the notfull/sval consistency part of the DEBUGASSERT in mcan_txready(). sama5's mcan_txready() (line 3162) has the identical pre-fix block: it reads SAM_MCAN_TXFQS, derives notfull from MCAN_TXFQS_TFQF, and asserts ((notfull && sval > 0) || (!notfull && sval <= 0)) at lines 3195-3196 under CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES. The same race exists there: txfsem is posted only by mcan_buffer_release(), which mcan_interrupt() calls on TX completion (line 3838), and sama5's mcan_buffer_reserve() has the same resynchronisation (nxsem_reset to 0 or to the FIFO free level) that the commit relies on. Nothing in the change is SAMv7-specific (same register, same bit, same semaphore and config field), so the false assertion can also trigger on sama5 under sustained CAN TX load in debug builds.
impact_note: The check is compiled only with CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES and halts only builds with debug assertions enabled; release builds behave the same, and the commit itself says "technically it's not a big issue".
title: The SAMA5 MCAN debug check in mcan_txready() can fire falsely when the TX FIFO frees a slot before the TX-complete interrupt has posted the semaphore.
summary: In September 2026 the samv7 MCAN driver relaxed the debug assertion in mcan_txready() so that it only checks that the semaphore count does not exceed the FIFO size, because the hardware can report a free TX FIFO slot before the interrupt handler has incremented txfsem. The sama5 MCAN driver has the same code and still asserts that the FIFO-not-full flag and the semaphore count agree. With CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES and debug assertions enabled, keeping the CAN TX queue full (for example when sending large data) can make the assertion fire and halt the system although nothing is wrong. Release builds are not affected, and the samv7 change can be copied as is.

subject: Fix #11005

Nothing makes this inapplicable to efm32: USBDEV_DMA in drivers/usbdev/Kconfig depends only on USBDEV, efm32_usbdev.c wires both functions into its ops table under CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA, and struct efm32_ep_s has the epphy field.

title: The EFM32 USB device driver uses an undeclared variable privep in its DMA buffer alloc/free functions, so it fails to build with USB DMA and USB tracing enabled.
summary: In October 2023 the stm32 OTG HS device driver fixed its allocbuffer/freebuffer functions, which referred to a local variable privep that is never declared, by casting the ep argument instead. The efm32 USB device driver has the same two functions with the same undeclared privep at lines 4389 and 4410. With CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA and either USB tracing or USB debug output enabled, usbtrace() is a real call and efm32_usbdev.c stops compiling; without tracing the bad expression is dropped by the macro. The stm32 change can be copied with only the struct name changed to efm32_ep_s.

subject: arch/mips/pic32mz: convert the Ethernet driver to netdev_lowerhalf.
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit "arch/mips/pic32mz: convert the Ethernet driver to netdev_lowerhalf." says it converts the driver "from the legacy net_driver_s model to the netdev_lowerhalf_s model", that "The RX descriptor ring handling and the TX done fixes already in the driver are kept", and that the buffer list, poll, response and txavail logic "are no longer needed and are removed". The selected hunks are mechanical parts of that conversion: the driver struct swaps pd_pollwork, pd_freebuffers and the net_driver_s for a mutex, a per-descriptor TX packet array and a netdev_lowerhalf_s; the prototypes change to the lower-half operations; and NETDEV_RXERRORS/NETDEV_TXERRORS(&priv->pd_dev) become (&priv->pd_dev.netdev) only because pd_dev changed type. pic32mx_ethernet.c still consistently uses the legacy model (struct net_driver_s pd_dev at line 312, devif_poll() at line 1187, d_txavail at line 3195, netdev_register() at line 3232), so there &priv->pd_dev is already the correct argument to the statistics macros. Carrying this over would be a driver-model conversion (refactor/new feature), not a missed bug fix.

title: The cxd56 USB device driver still throws away IN requests submitted while the endpoint is halted, so a mass-storage status reply can be lost.
summary: On 2026-07-28 the rp2040 and rp23xx USB device drivers stopped rejecting IN requests that arrive while an endpoint is halted: they now keep them queued and send them once the host clears the halt, because the mass storage class submits its status reply (CSW) while bulk-IN is still halted. The cxd56 driver still rejects such requests with -EBUSY in cxd56_epsubmit(), and its resume path only clears the STALL bit. The CXD56 does not declare stall queueing, so the mass storage class falls back to a 100 ms sleep workaround; if the host clears the halt later than that, the status reply is dropped and the host waits, times out and resets the device (the commit reports this with macOS). The fix has to be rewritten for this different controller, which starts IN transfers from an IN-token interrupt and can also clear the halt in hardware; how this controller treats a STALL while NAK is cleared cannot be checked from the repository.

title: The RISC-V RP23xx USB device driver still throws away IN requests submitted while the endpoint is halted, so a mass-storage status reply can be lost.
summary: On 2026-07-28 the arm rp2040 and rp23xx USB device drivers were changed to keep IN requests that arrive while an endpoint is halted and send them once the host clears the halt, because the mass storage class submits its status reply (CSW) while bulk-IN is still halted. The RISC-V build of the same RP23xx chip uses its own copy of the driver, which still rejects those requests with -EBUSY in rp23xx_epsubmit() and does not restart anything when the halt clears; its chip option also does not declare stall queueing. With a host that clears the halt later than the mass storage class's 100 ms workaround allows (the commit reports macOS), the status reply is lost, the host times out and resets the device, and the volume never mounts. The port needs the epsubmit change plus the matching re-arm on halt clear (and preferably the related halt-time cancel), written for this copy's spinlock-based locking rather than copied line for line.

subject: arch/xtensa/esp32s3: fix USB OTG request lifecycle on SMP
label: not_applicable
evidence: The commit is "arch/xtensa/esp32s3: fix USB OTG request lifecycle on SMP" and says "Without this, an SMP build can hang when a host opens the CDC ACM port while the target is continuously sending IN data"; ESP32-S3 selects ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU (arch/xtensa/Kconfig line 113) and SMP depends on it (sched/Kconfig line 416), but ARCH_CHIP_AT32 (arch/arm/Kconfig lines 1009-1021, one Cortex-M4) does not, and at32_otgfsdev.c has no spinlock at all. So the listed spin_lock_irqsave() additions to at32_req_remfirst() (line 980) and at32_req_addlast() (line 1007) have nothing to guard here: on one CPU the task side already changes the queue inside enter_critical_section() (at32_ep_submit, lines 4554 and 4566), which keeps the interrupt handler out. The hunk that keeps only EP0 on the early completion path (line 1473) and the usbreset hunk (next to line 2135) rely on the inflight/inflight_len/sent bookkeeping and XFRC-time completion added elsewhere in the commit, which AT32 does not have; in AT32 the bytes are already copied into the TxFIFO by at32_epin_transfer() (line 1447) before completion, and privep->active stays true until XFRC (line 1453) so at32_ep_submit() only queues the next request, which is the design stated at line 1477 and which the commit itself keeps for EP0. The NULL return added after DEBUGASSERT (line 1961) guards the new SMP/XFRC completion paths; the AT32 callers check the queue first, apart from the CONFIG_USBDEV_ISOCHRONOUS incomplete-IN handler (line 3527), a case the commit does not mention.

title: AT32 Ethernet promiscuous mode still blocks non-PAUSE control frames, so link-local multicast such as PTP may never reach the host.
summary: On 2026-09-21 the shared STM32 F1/F2/F4 Ethernet driver (stm32_eth_m3m4_v1.c, commit d357c5454) changed its promiscuous-mode frame filter to ETH_MACFFR_PCF_ALL so that all control frames are forwarded and link-local PTP multicast reaches the DMA. at32_eth.c still uses (ETH_MACFFR_PCF_PAUSE | ETH_MACFFR_PM) under CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS and programs MACFFR the same way, with identical PCF definitions in its header. With promiscuous mode enabled, frames the MAC treats as control frames (per the commit, including link-local PTP multicast) are dropped before they reach the network stack or packet sockets, so L2 PTP or similar link-local protocols run over packet sockets would not receive them. Confidence is limited because AT32 has no hardware PTP support in this driver, the problem only exists with CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS, and the effect on PTP frames is stated only by the commit message and the header comments, not by anything visible for this chip.

With LPI2C DMA enabled, a zero-length I2C message becomes a data TCD with iter 0; this would raise the configuration error, end that transfer with -EIO, and with HAE stop servicing all eDMA channels, since the driver has no code that clears HALT. Whether applications actually send zero-length I2C messages is not visible in this repository, and nothing was run on hardware.

subject: samv7: ensure the correct location of message RAM
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunks are the driver half of a real fix: SAMv7 put g_mcan0_msgram/g_mcan1_msgram into a '.mcan' section that its board linker scripts place at the start of .data (the start of SRAM, after an optional RAM vector table), because each buffer start is programmed as a 16-bit offset under one shared upper-16-bit base, and with a message RAM crossing a 64 KB boundary 'MCAN would sent data located at 0x20400000 to the network' (commit message). The SAMA5 copy uses the same addressing: MAILBOX_ADDRESS keeps only the low 16 bits (line 700), and sam_mcan_initialize() writes a single MSB taken from msgram.stdfilters into SFR_CAN (lines 4342 and 4366; hardware/sam_sfr.h line 249 'Bits 0-15: MSB CAN0 Base Address'), exactly like the SAMv7 MATRIX CAN0DMABA write. Its message RAM arrays (lines 998-1003 and 1089-1094) are still plain .bss arrays with only cache-line alignment, and nothing in the driver checks that they stay inside one 64 KB window, so the same failure can occur when the link places an array across a boundary. The fix must be adapted: no SAMA5 board linker script has a .mcan section, and e.g. sama5d2-xult uboot.ld puts .data right after .text in SDRAM, so 'start of .data' is not 64 KB aligned as SRAM start is on SAMv7; the zero-initialization part adds little because the arrays stay in .bss, which arm_data_initialize() already clears. Confidence is medium because the commit itself says the issue 'is not described anywhere in the manual' and whether a given SAMA5 image straddles a boundary depends on its layout.
title: The SAMA5 MCAN message RAM arrays are not kept inside one 64 KB window, although the controller only gets 16-bit buffer offsets under a single upper-16-bit base.
summary: In February 2025 (commit ef469bac) the SAMv7 MCAN driver moved its message RAM arrays into a '.mcan' section at the start of .data and zero-initialized them, because buffers lying past a 64 KB boundary were accessed at the wrong address and wrong data went out on the CAN bus. The SAMA5 copy of the driver programs the same 16-bit offsets and a single upper-16-bit base in SFR_CAN, but its g_mcan0_msgram and g_mcan1_msgram are still ordinary arrays placed wherever the linker puts them. If an array crosses a 64 KB boundary, the filters, receive FIFOs or transmit buffers after the boundary are read and written at the wrong memory address, so frames could be sent with wrong data or received into unrelated memory. The SAMv7 change cannot be copied as is, because SAMA5 linker scripts have no .mcan section and .data does not start on a 64 KB boundary there; a SAMA5-specific placement or alignment is needed. The commit notes the behaviour is not documented in the manual, so a hardware check on SAMA5 would confirm it.

subject: Fix compilation and fix SAM_DMAC_CHINTENCLR settings
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunk is the 'Fix compilation' part of the commit: in 'locate_data(".lpram"), aligned(16);' the comma ends the first declarator, so 'aligned(16)' is parsed as a second declarator with a number as its parameter list, which is not valid C; the fix writes 'locate_data(".lpram") aligned_data(16);' instead. For GCC, include/nuttx/compiler.h defines aligned_data(n) as __attribute__((aligned(n))) (line 368) and locate_data(n) as __attribute__((section(n))) (line 372), and there is no macro named 'aligned' that could make the old text valid. samd5e5/sam_dmac.c has the identical declarations of g_base_desc, g_writeback_desc and g_dma_desc (lines 141, 143 and 151), and Make.defs compiles that file whenever CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC is set (lines 72-73), so it fails to build under the same condition. No in-tree samd5e5 defconfig enables SAMD5E5_DMAC, which may be why the error is unnoticed; the CHINTENCLR change in the same commit is not part of this pair.
impact_note: The wrong declaration syntax only breaks compilation of sam_dmac.c when CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC is enabled; it cannot produce wrong runtime behaviour.
title: The SAMD5E5 DMA driver declares its LPRAM descriptor tables with invalid syntax and does not compile when DMA is enabled.
summary: In November 2023 (commit f5374e71) the SAMD2L2 DMA driver changed 'locate_data(".lpram"), aligned(16);' to 'locate_data(".lpram") aligned_data(16);' to fix the build. The SAMD5E5 copy still has the old text on all three descriptor tables (g_base_desc, g_writeback_desc and g_dma_desc), where the stray comma turns 'aligned(16)' into an invalid second declarator. As a result any configuration with CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC enabled fails to compile sam_dmac.c, so DMA cannot be used on SAMD5E5 until the same three-line change is made. No in-tree SAMD5E5 board configuration enables DMA, which is likely why this has not been reported.

subject: stm32h7:Serial refactor out tx dma semaphore
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The picked hunk only drops the 'if (status & DMA_SCR_HTIE) { nbytes += length / 2; }' branch of up_dma_txcallback(); the problem the commit describes ('The use of the semaphore was causing blocking on non blocking callers ... it left data in the xmit queue unsent') is fixed by its other hunks, which remove txdmasem and call up_dma_txavailable() at the end of the callback. The removed branch is for half-transfer interrupts, but the TX stream is always started with half = false (stm32f7 stm32_serial.c lines 3189-3190 and 3273, the same as stm32h7), and stm32_dmastart() then enables only DMA_SCR_TCIE | DMA_SCR_TEIE (stm32_dma.c line 809), so in normal operation the branch is never taken on either side. The only other way in is a DMA transfer error: the callback receives the stream's ISR flags (stm32_dma.c line 415), where DMA_STREAM_TEIF_BIT has the same value (1 << 3) as DMA_SCR_HTIE; the commit does not mention that case, and neither the old nor the new handling of it is clearly correct. So the picked hunk is a cleanup of an unused mode rather than the behavioural fix; stm32f7 never had txdmasem (its up_dma_txavailable() already tests stm32_dmaresidual(), line 3217), and whether it also needs the unpicked restart after uart_xmitchars_done() (line 3198) is outside this candidate and not judged here.

subject: arch/risc-v/espressif/i2s: Fix common driver issues
label: not_applicable
evidence: The picked hunks belong to a redesign of the Espressif buffer handling ('This commit refactors the I2S common driver for Espressif's RISC-V SoCs'): each container now gets heap-allocated lldesc_t descriptors (esp_i2s.c lines 255 and 559) and an internal DMA bounce buffer (lines 995 and 1120), so i2s_buf_free() must kmm_free() the descriptors and the RX worker frees bfcontainer->buf instead of the audio buffer, plus new master/slave channel-stop logic based on config->role, tx_en/rx_en and i2s_rx_channel_stop() (line 1520). rp2040_i2s.c matches only textually: its struct rp2040_buffer_s (lines 111-122) has no dma_link or buf member, nothing is allocated per container, and the driver is TX-only (g_i2sops at line 220 has no receive, no RX worker, no role or channel-stop functions). The lines matched at 555/559 are in rp2040's i2s_tx_worker(), where 'apb_free(bfcontainer->apb)' correctly releases the reference taken by 'apb_reference(apb)' in rp2040_i2s_send() (line 879); replacing it with a buffer free would be wrong. The remaining hunks only make i2s_buf_free() return the nxsem_post() result and log 'Failed to free buffer container' on the error path, which is not a behavioural fix for rp2040's void i2s_buf_free() at line 300.

subject: arch/risc-v/espressif/i2s: Fix common driver issues
label: not_applicable
evidence: The five candidate hunks of this Espressif RISC-V I2S refactor make i2s_buf_free return int and free heap-allocated lldesc_t DMA descriptors, return the nxsem_post result, replace apb_free(bfcontainer->apb) in the RX worker with kmm_free(bfcontainer->buf) plus a TX/RX channel-stop sequence, and log when i2s_buf_free fails. The return-type and logging parts do not change behaviour, and the descriptor freeing only pairs with the descriptor allocation that the same commit adds to i2s_buf_allocate (the old code embedded the descriptors in the container), so no pre-existing leak is fixed. The rp23xx driver is TX-only (its ops table has only TX methods and no receive), its buffer container has no dma_link or buf field, and its DMA reads straight from apb->samp, so there is no internal buffer or descriptor to free. The matching apb_free/i2s_buf_free lines sit in the TX worker and cleanup paths, where apb_free releases the reference taken by apb_reference in rp23xx_i2s_send, so the text match is not the same logic, and the channel-stop sequence relies on the ESP TX and RX channels sharing WS/BCLK, which this PIO-based TX-only driver does not have.

subject: arch/risc-v/espressif/i2s: Fix common driver issues
